name: Question 11
problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{2}\,\frac{dy}{dx}=3{y}^{4}+2xy,\,y(1)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the fact that the given differential equation can be transformed into the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+\frac{6}{x}\,z=-\frac{9}{{x}^{2}}
$$

using the substitution $z={y}^{-3}.$*

Solve the initial value problem x2dydx=3y4+2xy,y(1)=12.

Hint: You may wish to make use of the fact that the given differential equation can be transformed into the equation dzdx+6xz=−9x2 using the substitution z=y−3.

a
 y=x6x5+73
b
 y=x9−x53
c
 y=5x649−9x53
d
 y=3x25x3−13
e
 y=x212−4x53
